translated: I've never actually said I wanted to go to a shop like that, but I've always admired them.
Same here.
Yeah, some people really go around to all these different shaved ice shops, and... how should I put it?
It's not just your standard strawberry syrup. They have things like pumpkin cream shaved ice,
and it seems like they even have vegetable-based ones too.
Right? It's so fancy. And people who really love it will even eat it in the winter.
Shaved ice in the winter sounds nice too.
Doesn't it?
It's like eating ice cream in a warm room.
That sounds pretty good.
I'd love to try it sometime.
Definitely.
Did you go to any festivals?
I didn't go to any festivals.
I don't think I even happened to stumble across one this year.
I see. I actually went to a fireworks display, so I've been fully enjoying summer.
But I only looked at the shaved ice; I didn't actually eat any.
Oh, right, they have those food stalls and everything.
But when I went to Hokkaido like I mentioned earlier, I ate that famous melon topped with soft-serve ice cream.
As for ice cream... yeah, even at the airport on the way back—I flew home—well...
New Chitose Airport has so many shops selling soft-serve ice cream.
I carefully picked out one delicious one and ate it.
There are really that many?
So many.
I wouldn't be able to choose.
Exactly. So that's how it was.
I see.
I really want some shaved ice now.
Me too.
Thanks for the letter!
